title: Cylindrical object
spec: Create a new coordinate system by setting the Euler angles to negative ninety degrees around the X-axis, zero degrees around the Y-axis, and negative ninety degrees around the Z-axis. Ensure the translation vector is set to (0.0, 0.0, 0.0). Next, draw the first face of the cylindrical object. Start with the first loop by drawing an arc from (0.0, 0.0038) to (0.0011, 0.0011) and then to (0.0038, 0.0). Continue with a line from (0.0038, 0.0) to (0.0505, 0.0). Draw another arc from (0.0505, 0.0) to (0.0532, 0.0011) and then to (0.0543, 0.0038). Follow this with a line from (0.0543, 0.0038) to (0.0543, 0.0288). Draw an arc from (0.0543, 0.0288) to (0.0532, 0.0315) and then to (0.0505, 0.0326). Add a line from (0.0505, 0.0326) to (0.0038, 0.0326). Complete the loop with an arc from (0.0038, 0.0326) to (0.0011, 0.0315) and then to (0.0, 0.0288). Finally, draw a line from (0.0, 0.0288) back to (0.0, 0.0038). For the second loop, draw a line from (0.0022, 0.0022) to (0.0522, 0.0022), then from (0.0522, 0.0022) to (0.0522, 0.0304), from (0.0522, 0.0304) to (0.0022, 0.0304), and finally from (0.0022, 0.0304) back to (0.0022, 0.0022). Scale the entire 2D sketch by a factor of 0.0543. Transform the scaled 2D sketch into 3D by rotating it using the Euler angles specified in the coordinate system and translating it using the translation vector. Extrude the 2D sketch 0.75 units along the normal direction without extruding in the opposite direction. Create a new solid body from the extruded sketch. The final dimensions of the cylindrical object are length: 0.05434782608695652 units, width: 0.03260869565217391 units, and height: 0.75 units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0038) \
     .threePointArc((0.0011, 0.0011), (0.0038, 0.0)) \
     .lineTo(0.0505, 0.0) \
     .threePointArc((0.0532, 0.0011), (0.0543, 0.0038)) \
     .lineTo(0.0543, 0.0288) \
     .threePointArc((0.0532, 0.0315), (0.0505, 0.0326)) \
     .lineTo(0.0038, 0.0326) \
     .threePointArc((0.0011, 0.0315), (0.0, 0.0288)) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0038) \
     .close()

# Create the inner loop
r = r.moveTo(0.0022, 0.0022) \
     .lineTo(0.0522, 0.0022) \
     .lineTo(0.0522, 0.0304) \
     .lineTo(0.0022, 0.0304) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# Note: CAD-Query does not directly support Euler angles, but we can use rotate and translate methods
# The given Euler angles (-90, 0, -90) correspond to a rotation of 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# The translation vector is [0, 0, 0], so no translation is needed

# Final model
r  # This will represent the final model

import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the outer and inner loops of the sketch
outer_loop = [
    (0.0, 0.0),
    (0.0543, 0.0),
    (0.0543, 0.0326),
    (0.0, 0.0326),
    (0.0, 0.0)
]

inner_loop = [
    (0.0022, 0.0022),
    (0.0521, 0.0022),
    (0.0521, 0.0304),
    (0.0022, 0.0304),
    (0.0022, 0.0022)
]

# Create the sketch
r = r.polyline(outer_loop).close().polyline(inner_loop).close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# Note: CAD-Query does not directly support Euler angles, but we can use rotate and translate methods
# The given Euler angles (-90, 0, -90) correspond to a rotation of 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90).rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the outer rectangle
r = r.box(0.0543, 0.0326, 0.75, centered=(False, False, False))

# Define the inner rectangle
inner_rectangle = cq.Workplane("XY").box(0.0518, 0.0299, 0.75, centered=(False, False, False)).translate((0.0013, 0.0013, 0))

# Cut the inner rectangle from the outer rectangle
r = r.cut(inner_rectangle)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles are (-90, 0, -90) and the translation vector is (0, 0, 0)
# This transformation is equivalent to rotating the model 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90).rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)
